title: Design the Data Model

header.html: Configure table and column properties; Implement role-playing dimensions; Define a relationship's cardinality and cross-filter direction; Create a common date table; Identify use cases for calculated columns and calculated tables
the official PL-300 study guide (skills measured as of April 20, 2026)

html:
1Table and column properties

The data model is the set of tables, relationships and calculations behind your reports. Good design starts with the properties of each table and column, which you set in Model view, in the Properties pane or on the Column tools tab.

Property What it does Example
Data category Tells visuals how to treat the values City lets a map place it; Web URL makes a link
Sort by column Orders one column by another column of the same table Month Name sorted by Month Number
Default summarization How a field is aggregated when you drag it into a visual Sum, Average, Minimum, Maximum, Count, Count (Distinct) or Do not summarize
Format Display format, decimals and symbols Currency, percentage, date
Hide Removes the field from the Report view field list Hide keys and helper columns
Display folder Groups fields into folders in the Fields pane A folder named Sales Metrics
Description Text shown as a tooltip when you hover over the field Explains what a measure means
Is key Marks the column that uniquely identifies each row ProductKey in the Product table
Hierarchy An ordered set of columns for drill down Category, Subcategory, Product

Numeric columns default to Sum. That is wrong for keys and for a year column, so set them to Do not summarize (the menu label reads Don't summarize). A hierarchy needs all its columns in the same table, because hierarchies cannot span tables.

Exam tip

. Sort by column fixes a text column that sorts alphabetically, such as month names ordered by month number. Set keys and years to Do not summarize so they are not added up.

Exam tip

. A hidden field is hidden only from the Report view field list. It still works in relationships and DAX, and a user with Build permission on the semantic model can still see it.

2Role-playing dimensions

A role-playing dimension is one dimension used in more than one role. A Sales table with OrderDate and ShipDate relates to one Date table twice. Power BI allows only one active relationship between two tables. The active one is a solid line; the others are inactive and drawn dashed.

Approach How it works Trade-off
USERELATIONSHIP Keep one Date table; a measure turns on the inactive relationship inside CALCULATE Smaller model, but you need one measure per role, and a Date slicer filters only the active role
One dimension table per role (recommended) Create an Order Date and a Ship Date table, as referenced queries or calculated tables, and rename columns to be self-describing Every role has its own slicers and relationship; the model is slightly larger 
Sales by Ship Date =
CALCULATE (
    SUM ( Sales[Amount] ),
    USERELATIONSHIP ( Sales[ShipDate], 'Date'[Date] )
)
Exam tip

. Only one relationship between two tables can be active. An inactive one is used only inside a measure through USERELATIONSHIP. Microsoft recommends one dimension table per role.

3Cardinality and cross-filter direction

Cardinality describes how many rows match on each side of a relationship.

Cardinality Meaning Note
One-to-many One dimension row matches many fact rows Default in a star schema; fastest
Many-to-one The same relationship seen from the fact table Behaves the same
One-to-one Each row matches at most one row on the other side Always filters both ways; consider merging the tables
Many-to-many Neither column holds unique values Slowest; use a bridge table when you can

The column on the one side must be unique. Duplicate values there make the refresh fail, so add an index (surrogate key) column in Power Query if needed. Key columns on both sides need the same data type, and date keys should not carry a time part.

Cross-filter direction controls how filters travel.

Direction Behavior
Single Filters flow from the one side to the many side (default and recommended)
Both Filters flow in both directions; a one-to-one relationship is always Both

Both is risky. It can create ambiguous filter paths, slow the queries and give surprising totals. Prefer Single, and use the CROSSFILTER function inside one measure when you need Both only there. The setting Apply security filter in both directions exists only for row-level security. Assume referential integrity (DirectQuery, no NULLs on the many side) allows an inner join.

Exam tip

. Filters flow from the one side to the many side. Duplicates in the one-side column stop the refresh; a many-to-many relationship is the slowest; use Both only when a scenario truly needs it.

4Create a common date table

A common date table is one Date dimension that every fact table relates to. It is the foundation of time intelligence.

Requirement Detail
Dates Unique and contiguous: one row per day, no gaps, no duplicates
Nulls None
Data type Date or Date/Time, covering all the dates in your data
Mark as date table Table tools, then Mark as date table, then pick the Date column
Relationship One-to-many from the Date column to the fact table's date column, same type, no time part

CALENDAR builds a table from a start date and an end date you give. CALENDARAUTO finds the range from the date columns in the model; an optional argument sets the last month of the fiscal year, so CALENDARAUTO(6) fits a June year end. You can also build the table in Power Query or load it from the source.

Date =
ADDCOLUMNS (
    CALENDARAUTO (),
    "Year", YEAR ( [Date] ),
    "Month Number", MONTH ( [Date] ),
    "Month", FORMAT ( [Date], "mmmm" )
)

Auto date/time creates a hidden date table for every date column. This makes the model bigger, so turn it off in the Data Load options once you have a real date table. Marking your table as the date table removes the hidden one. A DirectQuery model has no automatic date hierarchy, so it needs a date table.

Exam tip

. CALENDAR needs a start and an end date; CALENDARAUTO detects the range and takes an optional fiscal year end month. Mark the table as the date table, and turn auto date/time off to keep the model small.

5Calculated columns and calculated tables

Object When it is computed Best use
Calculated column Per row, at refresh; stored in the model and uses memory A value you filter, group, slice or relate by
Measure At query time, in the filter context; nothing stored Totals, ratios and other aggregations
Calculated table A DAX table expression stored in the model; recalculated when its source tables refresh Date table, role-playing copy, bridge or helper table
Power Query custom column During refresh, as part of loading Preferred when possible

Power Query is preferred when possible. Its columns compress better and are part of the refresh. Use DAX when you need a measure or a DAX-only function, such as RELATED, or logic that depends on other tables in the model. A calculated column can be used in a slicer, an axis, a filter or a relationship; a measure cannot.

Exam tip

. A calculated column is stored and computed per row; a measure is computed at query time. If a value goes on an axis or slicer it must be a column; if it is a total that reacts to filters it must be a measure.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A matrix shows month names in alphabetical order, so April comes before January. The Date table also has a Month Number column. What should you do?

  • AMark the Date table as the date table in the model
  • BSet Month Name to sort by the Month Number column
  • CSet the Data category of Month Name to Uncategorized
  • DChange the default summarization of Month Name to Minimum
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Sort by column property orders a text column by a numeric column of the same table, and the other options do not change the sort order.

S2A Sales table has OrderDate and ShipDate, and both relate to one Date table with OrderDate as the active relationship. A measure must total sales by ship date. What should you use?

  • ACALCULATE with USERELATIONSHIP on the ShipDate column
  • BCALCULATE with CROSSFILTER on the OrderDate column
  • CA calculated column with RELATED on the ShipDate column
  • DCALCULATE with ALL on the Date table before summing
Show the answer

Answer: A. USERELATIONSHIP turns on the inactive relationship for the duration of that calculation.

S3An author sets every relationship in a star schema to Both so that all filters reach all tables. What is the most likely result?

  • ARefresh fails because the dimension keys are duplicated
  • BRow-level security no longer applies to any report viewer
  • CAmbiguous filter paths and slower queries in large models
  • DThe inactive relationships become active at the same time
Show the answer

Answer: C. Bi-directional filtering can create ambiguity and hurt performance, so Single is the better default.

S4A finance team's fiscal year ends in June. You need a Date table that covers every date in the model. Which expression should you use?

  • ACALENDAR with the number six as the first argument
  • BDATESYTD with the number six as the year end date
  • CPARALLELPERIOD with six months as the interval
  • DCALENDARAUTO with six as the fiscal year end month
Show the answer

Answer: D. CALENDARAUTO finds the date range itself and accepts the last month of the fiscal year.

S5A Customer table gets its data from a SQL view. A DAX calculated column that joins FirstName and LastName inflates the model. What should you do?

  • ABuild the same logic as a Power Query column
  • BMove the same logic into a new calculated table
  • CRewrite the same logic as a measure in the model
  • DSet the column to Do not summarize and hide it
Show the answer

Answer: A. Power Query columns compress better than DAX calculated columns and are built in at refresh, so they are preferred when possible.

S6Report users want to drill from Category to Subcategory to Product in one visual. All three columns are in the Product table. What should you create?

  • AA display folder that holds the three columns
  • BA hierarchy that holds the three columns
  • CA relationship from the table to itself
  • DA calculated table that unions the columns
Show the answer

Answer: B. A hierarchy orders columns of one table for drill down, whereas a display folder only groups fields in the Fields pane.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which property sorts Month Name by Month Number?

Show the answer

Sort by column.

R2How many active relationships can exist between two tables?

Show the answer

One.

R3Which function turns on an inactive relationship inside a measure?

Show the answer

USERELATIONSHIP.

R4What are the two cross-filter directions?

Show the answer

Single and Both.

R5Which DAX function builds a date table from the dates already in the model?

Show the answer

CALENDARAUTO.

R6When is a calculated column computed, and where is it kept?

Show the answer

At refresh, and it is stored in the model.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Column properties Data category, Sort by column, Default summarization (Do not summarize for keys), Format, Hide, Display folder, Description, Is key
Hierarchy Columns of one table only; used for drill down
Role-playing One active relationship only; USERELATIONSHIP for the others; one table per role is recommended
Cardinality One-to-many is the default and fastest; the one side must be unique; many-to-many is slowest
Direction Single by default (one side to many side); Both can be ambiguous and slow
Date table Unique, contiguous dates, no nulls, marked as date table; CALENDAR or CALENDARAUTO; turn off auto date/time
Calculated column Per row, stored, usable on axes, slicers and relationships
Measure and table Measure at query time; calculated table stored; Power Query preferred
